trust_decision.summary: Which namespace a lease operation acts in: the request is ACL-checked in the caller's (or re-routed) namespace, but at the pinned commit loadEntry silently switches to the namespace embedded in the lease ID, and the request router only re-routes body-form lease IDs, so the ACL namespace and the storage namespace can differ.

landing_point.why: Summary names canonical sys/leases/{revoke,renew}; handleRevoke/handleRenew are the handlers, and the url_lease_id fallback at vault/logical_system.go:2046-2049 is the obvious path-segment variant. The router special-case at vault/request_handling.go:935 is the second obvious stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST sys/leases/revoke/<lease_id>, sys/leases/renew/<lease_id> (path-segment form now re-routed by embedded ns ID; body form kept)
every ExpirationManager lease load: sys/leases/revoke[/id], sys/leases/renew[/id], sys/leases/revoke-prefix/<id>, sys/leases/revoke-force/<id> (removal of the lease-ID namespace override)
POST sys/leases/lookup (and auth/token lookup via FetchLeaseTimesByToken) served from the pending/irrevocable in-memory cache
fix_sites.module_kind: cache fast path in expiration manager

fix_sites.entry_point: sys/leases/renew[/id] (redundant cross-namespace check removed now that loadEntry no longer crosses)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: vault/expiration.go:2105-2116 (loadEntry), reached by sys/leases/revoke-prefix/<id> and revoke-force/<id> via vault/expiration.go:1265-1274; plus the cache fast path vault/expiration.go:1808-1816 for sys/leases/lookup

O3_reason_to_dismiss: revoke-prefix/revoke-force are sudo-only prefix endpoints (vault/logical_system.go:83-84) that 'take a mount prefix, not a lease ID', and lookup is read-only and already re-routed by body lease_id, so a solver fixing the router for revoke/renew path segments can argue those are a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate cross-namespace lease ops must keep working: a request sent to a parent namespace with a child-namespace token/lease is re-routed by the lease's embedded ns ID (fix test cases 'root->ns1 via ns1 token', 'ns2->ns1 via ns1 token'); internal revocation (RevokeByToken, expiry timers with nsCtx) still loads leases. A solver who hard-rejects any request-ns != lease-ns, or drops the router re-routing, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: lease_id as URL path segment (sys/leases/{renew,revoke}/<id>), body taking precedence
non-string lease_id in body (rejected as invalid lease ID instead of panicking type assertion)
non-string token in body for auth/token/* re-routing
lease ID with vs without embedded namespace suffix (root lease looked up from a child namespace via cache)

O7_producer.where: vault/expiration.go:1808-1816 (pending/irrevocable maps returning cachedLeaseInfo without consulting request namespace); the namespace is attached at load time in vault/expiration.go:2147

O8b_injection_room.sibling: revokePrefixCommon's single-lease shortcut could re-derive the namespace from the lease ID suffix itself (as loadEntry did) so revoke-prefix/<foreign id> keeps crossing after a router-only fix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'helpful' convenience as the removed loadEntry block; a maintainer wanting revoke-prefix to accept a fully-qualified lease ID would write exactly this.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: FetchLeaseTimesByToken-style helper that reads lease info from the pending cache by token-derived ID without a namespace check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The cache fast path is an optimisation maintainers copy into new lookup helpers; it never sees the request namespace.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: handleLeaseLookupList accepting a prefix with an embedded ns ID and listing that namespace's leaseView
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the router's embedded-ns re-routing that already exists for lookup/renew/revoke.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the router switch at vault/request_handling.go:935 to also re-route sys/leases/{revoke,renew}/<id> path segments, leaving loadEntry's lease-ID namespace override (revoke-prefix/revoke-force) and the lookup cache fast path open.

out_of_scope_notes: Predecessor CVE-2026-45808 (changelog/3152.txt:2) removed legacy sys/revoke*, sys/renew endpoints; this advisory is its incomplete-fix sibling.
Pinned token re-routing does token.(string) on arbitrary body data (vault/request_handling.go:901); fix hardens it but it is a panic-shape issue, not the namespace protection.
sys/leases/revoke-force is listed as an exact path at vault/request_handling.go:935 but the route pattern requires a prefix (vault/logical_system_paths.go:2765), so that case was dead code.
